hypothesis_1_biofouling_trajectory_predi.claim: The RATE of biofouling accumulation predicts time-to-obstruction. A causal model maps biofouling trajectory → hydraulic degradation → time-to-functional failure.

closest_prior_art.overlap: LOW — CGM sensors degrade via enzyme inactivation, not biofouling. Different mechanism, different device.
MODERATE — ML for biofouling prediction exists in marine/industrial context. But NOT for medical shunt time-to-obstruction.
closest_prior_art.threat: LOW-MODERATE — establishes ML+biofouling is known, but not in shunt context

closest_prior_art.source: Hybrid models, digital twins for fouling prediction (industrial)
closest_prior_art.overlap: LOW — industrial fouling (heat exchangers, ships), not medical implants
LOW — different implant (joint prosthesis), different degradation mechanism (wear, not biofouling)

hypothesis_1_biofouling_trajectory_predi.rationale: No patent or publication found for biofouling-rate-trajectory-based time-to-obstruction prediction in CSF shunt systems. Biofouling prediction exists in marine/industrial contexts but NOT in medical shunts. The specific causal model (biofouling rate → resistance trajectory → time-to-obstruction) for shunt failure prediction is NOT found.

hypothesis_2_failure_mode_discrimination.claim: Different obstruction causes (biofouling, tissue ingrowth, blood clot, debris) produce different sensor signatures. The system can classify WHICH type of obstruction is developing.

closest_prior_art.source: Ventricular catheter tissue obstruction and shunt malfunction (PMC)
closest_prior_art.overlap: LOW — academic study correlating tissue obstruction degree with malfunction. Does NOT use sensor signatures to discriminate causes. Is imaging-based, not sensor-based.
MODERATE — reviews smart catheters with embedded sensors. BUT: focuses on general sensing (pressure, flow, pH), NOT on obstruction-cause discrimination.

closest_prior_art.source: Early warning sensor for catheter encrustation (urinary)
closest_prior_art.overlap: MODERATE — detects encrustation (one type of blockage) via pH. BUT: detects ONE cause, does NOT discriminate between multiple causes.
closest_prior_art.threat: LOW — single-cause detection, not multi-cause discrimination

closest_prior_art.source: US11865241B2 — Sensor monitoring for in-dwelling catheter
closest_prior_art.overlap: LOW — general catheter monitoring, not obstruction-cause discrimination

hypothesis_2_failure_mode_discrimination.rationale: No patent or publication found for MULTI-CAUSE obstruction discrimination in shunt systems using sensor signatures. Existing systems detect ONE type of blockage (encrustation, biofouling, flow reduction). Nobody discriminates BETWEEN causes (biofouling vs tissue ingrowth vs blood clot vs debris) using sensor pattern analysis.

light_simulation_failure_mode_discrimina.question: Can biofouling sensor signatures distinguish between biofouling obstruction, tissue ingrowth, blood clot, and debris obstruction?
light_simulation_failure_mode_discrimina.method: Simulate 4 obstruction types with different biofouling sensor signatures. Train ML classifier. Measure discrimination accuracy.

blood_clot.impedance_signature: sudden large impedance jump, high frequency burst

debris.impedance_signature: noisy, variable impedance, no clear trend

simulation_parameters.ml_model: Random Forest (100 trees, depth 8), 5-fold Stratified CV
simulation_parameters.features: impedance mean, std, trend, max, min, rate_of_change, burst_ratio, frequency_content_estimate
